key_insight: A lone-pair-driven lattice-softness strategy can suppress phonon transport to achieve ultralow thermal conductivity in hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites.
engineering_relevance: This provides a materials-design route for thermoelectric and thermal-management applications where minimizing heat flow is critical.
method: Physics-guided symbolic-regression machine learning to identify lone-pair-dominated compositions
Thermal, electrical, impedance, and DFT characterization of structure-transport relationships
evidence_signal: GuaPbI3 shows an ultralow room-temperature thermal conductivity of 0.088 W m^-1 K^-1, with bulk-dominated transport and bias-dependent conductivity.
watch_item: The electronically active transport appears sensitive to bias and chemical potential, so device performance may be strongly condition-dependent.
paper_title: Lone-Pair-Induced Lattice Softness Enables Ultralow Thermal Conductivity in Hybrid Organic-Inorganic Perovskite GuaPbI$_3$
